notes: 30 Hard + 20 Normal. Hard continues the batch-007 method: named settlements and junctions on long-distance routes, sparse views. The 20 Normal are composed to protect the tightest Normal balance gate — rural+remote sits at 18.3% against a 15% floor, so Normal here is 8 rural / 6 suburban / 6 urban, which raises every Normal ratio or holds it. No panoId appears here: one may only come from a real verification run.

candidates.label: Solitaire, C14
candidates.source: C14 gravel road at the Solitaire settlement, Namib desert.
candidates.rationale: Hard: a fuel pump and two buildings in open desert. Namibia's first catalog entry, and about as clueless a view as the tier allows.

candidates.label: Ghanzi, A2
candidates.source: A2 Trans-Kalahari highway through Ghanzi, western Botswana.
candidates.rationale: Hard: Kalahari sand and thorn scrub around a low-rise district town. Moved from Kang, which the cross-batch check found 230 m from botswana-kalahari-highway, a batch-001 ZERO_RESULTS.

candidates.label: Hoop Street, Calvinia
candidates.source: Hoop Street through Calvinia, Hantam Karoo, Northern Cape.
candidates.rationale: Hard: a wide dusty street under bare Hantam escarpment, almost no vegetation. Replaces a Springbok candidate that the collision check found 600 m from the existing N7 Namaqualand entry.

candidates.label: Mokhotlong, A1
candidates.source: A1 at Mokhotlong, eastern Lesotho highlands.
candidates.rationale: Hard: 2400 m treeless highland with scattered stone building. 150 km from the A2 Mafeteng entry and far barer.

candidates.label: Midelt, N13
candidates.source: N13 through Midelt, between the Middle and High Atlas.
candidates.rationale: Hard: high desert plain under bare mountains, minimal signage. Morocco lost its only entry when Jemaa el-Fnaa failed; this is a genuinely hard replacement rather than a landmark.

candidates.label: Kegen, A351
candidates.source: A351 at Kegen, Almaty region.
candidates.rationale: Hard: steppe under the Tian Shan with Soviet-era low building. Kazakhstan's first entry; visually close to the Kyrgyz entries, which is a fair trap.

candidates.label: Tsetserleg, A0501
candidates.source: A0501 through Tsetserleg, Arkhangai province.
candidates.rationale: Hard: a small provincial capital of low concrete on open steppe. Mongolia missed once on an unnamed steppe point; a named aimag centre is where coverage actually is.

candidates.label: Kutchan, Route 5
candidates.source: National Route 5 through Kutchan, Hokkaido.
candidates.rationale: Hard: snow-country low-rise with high roadside snow poles. Reads as northern Europe until the Japanese signage is spotted.

candidates.label: Jeongseon, Route 42
candidates.source: National Route 42 at Jeongseon, Gangwon.
candidates.rationale: Hard: steep forested valley with a small riverside town. None of the urban Korean cues the catalog's other Korean entries provide.

candidates.label: Fenqihu, County Route 169
candidates.source: County Route 169 at Fenqihu, Chiayi county.
candidates.rationale: Hard: cloud-forest mountain road with bamboo and tea. Subtropical highland that could be anywhere from Yunnan to northern Vietnam.

candidates.label: Tanah Rata, Route 59
candidates.source: Route 59 through Tanah Rata, Cameron Highlands.
candidates.rationale: Hard: tea slopes and mist at 1500 m — cool highland vegetation that hides the tropical latitude entirely.

candidates.label: Bajawa, Trans-Flores Highway
candidates.source: Trans-Flores Highway at Bajawa, Flores.
candidates.rationale: Hard: upland volcanic country with corrugated roofs and little signage. 1400 km from the Java entries and nothing like them.

candidates.label: Bontoc, Halsema Highway
candidates.source: Halsema Highway at Bontoc, Mountain Province.
candidates.rationale: Hard: steep Cordillera terrain with sparse building and few signs. 100 km from Baguio and far more remote.

candidates.label: Leh bazaar road, NH3
candidates.source: NH3 through Leh, Ladakh.
candidates.rationale: Hard: high-altitude desert with Tibetan-influenced building. India lost its India Gate entry; this restores the country with a view that gives nothing away — most players will guess Tibet or Nepal.

candidates.label: Besisahar, Lamjung
candidates.source: The Besisahar road at Lamjung district headquarters.
candidates.rationale: Hard: mid-hill Himalayan town, concrete and corrugated iron, Devanagari signage. Nepal's first entry; easily confused with northern India.

candidates.label: Shoshoni, US 20
candidates.source: US 20 at Shoshoni, Wyoming.
candidates.rationale: Hard: high desert junction with a handful of buildings. 130 km from the Jeffrey City candidate, so a separate cluster.

candidates.label: Van Horn, US 90
candidates.source: US 90 through Van Horn, west Texas.
candidates.rationale: Hard: Chihuahuan desert and a motel strip. Visually continuous with northern Mexico 100 km south.

candidates.label: Hearst, Highway 11
candidates.source: Highway 11 through Hearst, northern Ontario.
candidates.rationale: Hard: boreal forest and a francophone mill town. The French signage misleads toward Quebec, 900 km east.

candidates.label: Guerrero Negro, Mex 1
candidates.source: Mex 1 at Guerrero Negro, Baja California Sur.
candidates.rationale: Hard: salt flats and coastal desert. 400 km from the Cataviña entry on the same highway but a different cluster and a different landscape.

candidates.label: Chaitén, Carretera Austral
candidates.source: Ruta 7 through Chaitén, Los Lagos.
candidates.rationale: Hard: temperate rainforest and volcanic ash, low tin-roofed building. 360 km from the Cerro Castillo candidate.

candidates.label: Gobernador Gregores, Ruta 40
candidates.source: RN40 through Gobernador Gregores, Santa Cruz.
candidates.rationale: Hard: Patagonian steppe town, wind, gravel, one fuel station. Replaces a Perito Moreno candidate that the collision check found 200 m from the existing RN40 Patagonia entry — that entry is already in that town.

candidates.label: Avenida Regimiento Chichas, Tupiza
candidates.source: Avenida Regimiento Chichas through Tupiza, Potosí department.
candidates.rationale: Hard: a dusty town under red desert canyons, low adobe and brick. Moved from Uyuni, which the cross-batch check found 370 m from bolivia-altiplano-uyuni, a batch-001 ZERO_RESULTS.

candidates.label: Abancay, PE-3S
candidates.source: PE-3S through Abancay, Apurímac.
candidates.rationale: Hard: steep valley town with dense low concrete. 200 km from Cusco and without any of its recognisable architecture.

candidates.label: Mocoa, Ruta 45
candidates.source: Ruta 45 at Mocoa, Putumayo.
candidates.rationale: Hard: Amazon-piedmont town, heavy green, low building. Could be Ecuador or Peru without a sign.

candidates.label: Alcântara, MA-106
candidates.source: MA-106 at Alcântara, Maranhão.
candidates.rationale: Hard: equatorial coast with sparse colonial ruin and palm. 2000 km from the Minas rural entry.

candidates.label: Filadelfia, Ruta 9
candidates.source: Ruta 9 Transchaco at Filadelfia, Boquerón.
candidates.rationale: Hard: Chaco thorn scrub with a grid-planned Mennonite settlement. Paraguay's first entry and one of the least readable views on the continent.

candidates.label: Roberts Street, Norseman
candidates.source: Roberts Street, Norseman, at the western end of the Eyre Highway.
candidates.rationale: Hard: goldfields scrub and a wide empty street. The Nullarbor and Ceduna points both failed as unnamed highway coordinates; this is the named town at the same end of the route.

candidates.label: Brodie Street, Hughenden
candidates.source: Brodie Street, Hughenden, Flinders Highway, Queensland.
candidates.rationale: Hard: dry inland Queensland township. 210 km from the Winton entry, so a separate cluster, and equally featureless.

candidates.label: Murchison, SH6
candidates.source: SH6 through Murchison, Tasman.
candidates.rationale: Hard: a one-street river town in beech country. 240 km from the Haast entry on the same highway.

candidates.label: Ranfurly, SH85
candidates.source: SH85 through Ranfurly, Maniototo, Otago.
candidates.rationale: Hard: dry inland basin, tussock, almost no trees. 60 km from the Alexandra entry — outside the cluster radius and visually similar, which is the point.

candidates.label: Trần Phú street, Hội An
candidates.source: Trần Phú street in the old quarter of Hội An.
candidates.rationale: Normal, not easy: ochre shophouses and Vietnamese signage identify the country readily, but Hội An itself is not a globally recognised skyline. Vietnam's first entry after the Hanoi candidate failed.

candidates.label: Street 2, Battambang
candidates.source: Street 2 along the Sangkae river, central Battambang.
candidates.rationale: Normal: French-colonial shophouses and Khmer script. The script settles the country; nothing settles the city. 280 km from the Angkor entry.

candidates.label: Sisavangvong Road, Luang Prabang
candidates.source: Sisavangvong Road through the Luang Prabang peninsula.
candidates.rationale: Normal: low colonial shopfronts and temple walls. Distinctive to south-east Asia without being a landmark view; 200 km from the Vientiane entry.

candidates.label: Çarşı, Safranbolu
candidates.source: The Çarşı old market quarter of Safranbolu, Karabük.
candidates.rationale: Normal: Ottoman timber houses on a cobbled street. Strongly Turkish, weakly locatable — nothing like the Istanbul entry.

candidates.label: Vasileos Konstantinou, Nafplio
candidates.source: Vasileos Konstantinou street, central Nafplio, Peloponnese.
candidates.rationale: Normal: neoclassical frontage and Greek signage. The alphabet gives the country immediately; the town is one of dozens. Athens' Acropolis is the easy Greek view.

candidates.label: Corso Mazzini, Ascoli Piceno
candidates.source: Corso Mazzini through central Ascoli Piceno, Marche.
candidates.rationale: Normal: travertine facades on an ordinary corso. Unmistakably Italian, entirely unplaceable within Italy.

candidates.label: Rue Gambetta, Figeac
candidates.source: Rue Gambetta, central Figeac, Lot.
candidates.rationale: Normal: medieval stone and shutters in a small southern French town. French road furniture settles the country; the town does not announce itself.

candidates.label: Obermarkt, Görlitz
candidates.source: Obermarkt square, Görlitz, on the Polish border.
candidates.rationale: Normal, and a good trap: the architecture is as much Silesian as German and Poland begins 300 m east. Nothing here says Berlin.

candidates.label: Strada Nicolae Bălcescu, Sibiu
candidates.source: Strada Nicolae Bălcescu, the central pedestrian street of Sibiu.
candidates.rationale: Normal: Saxon burgher architecture with Romanian signage — a combination that misleads toward Austria or Hungary. Romania's first entry after Viscri failed.

candidates.label: Stefan Stambolov street, Veliko Tarnovo
candidates.source: Stefan Stambolov street through central Veliko Tarnovo.
candidates.rationale: Normal: Cyrillic signage on a steep hillside town. The script narrows to the Balkans or Russia, which is real work for the player. Bulgaria's first entry.

candidates.label: Námestie SNP, Banská Bystrica
candidates.source: Námestie SNP, the central square of Banská Bystrica.
candidates.rationale: Normal: a Central European square that is very hard to separate from Czechia or Poland. Slovakia's first entry.

candidates.label: Great George Street, Charlottetown
candidates.source: Great George Street, Charlottetown, Prince Edward Island.
candidates.rationale: Normal: brick and clapboard on a quiet Maritime street. Easily mistaken for New England. 170 km from the Moncton entry.

candidates.label: Main Street, Bisbee
candidates.source: Main Street through Bisbee, Arizona.
candidates.rationale: Normal: a mining town built into a canyon, brick frontage, desert hills. American but not identifiable as such at a glance — the catalog's other US entries are all instantly readable.

candidates.label: Avenida Philippi, Frutillar
candidates.source: Avenida Philippi along the lakefront at Frutillar, Los Lagos.
candidates.rationale: Normal: German-settler timber architecture beside a lake and volcano. The architecture argues for central Europe and the volcano against it, which is exactly the tension normal wants.

candidates.label: Calle Belgrano, Tilcara
candidates.source: Calle Belgrano through Tilcara, Quebrada de Humahuaca, Jujuy.
candidates.rationale: Normal: adobe village in a coloured desert canyon. Andean and Spanish-speaking, but Bolivia and Peru look much the same — the Jujuy candidate that failed earlier was an unnamed route point 80 km away.

candidates.label: Rua Direita, Tiradentes
candidates.source: Rua Direita, the main street of Tiradentes, Minas Gerais.
candidates.rationale: Normal: colonial whitewash and stone paving. Portuguese signage settles the country; the town is one of a dozen similar Minas villages.

candidates.label: Main Road, Hermanus
candidates.source: Main Road through Hermanus, Overberg, Western Cape.
candidates.rationale: Normal: a coastal town street with fynbos hills behind. 100 km from Cape Town and without the mountain that identifies it.

candidates.label: Avenue Hassan II, Chefchaouen
candidates.source: Avenue Hassan II along the edge of the Chefchaouen medina.
candidates.rationale: Normal: Rif mountain town with Arabic and French signage on an ordinary avenue. The blue-painted lanes that make the town famous are inside the medina and out of frame.

candidates.label: Mackay Street, Greymouth
candidates.source: Mackay Street, central Greymouth, West Coast.
candidates.rationale: Normal: a small wet-coast town of low commercial frontage under bush-covered hills. Left-hand traffic and vegetation give the country; nothing gives the island.

candidates.label: Katoomba Street, Katoomba
candidates.source: Katoomba Street, the main street of Katoomba, Blue Mountains, New South Wales.
candidates.rationale: Normal: a cool-climate mountain town of interwar shopfronts. The famous escarpment lookouts are 1.5 km south and out of frame, which keeps this off the easy tier.
